Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pdmS7 0.27.0

  • The modelled well level was 1000 times too flat. The depth to the water table is W = Ys D in metres, with the deficit D in mm and Ys in m per mm (PDM for PCs wellfac), as UKCEH’s Table 3 values need: with Ys 0.0204 and Smax_b 1641 mm the well ranges over 33.5 m. The core divided by a further 1000, so the well moved by centimetres. Only the well_level_m column changes; the flow does not. Ys is documented as the well factor, 1 / (1000 Sy) for a specific yield Sy, not as the specific yield itself.
  • fit_well_level() fits ys and hw to an observed well by least squares on the modelled storage, after the flow is calibrated, with print and plot methods.
  • Using the groundwater extension, a new how-to article: when the extension is needed, preparing abstraction and well records, setting it up, calibrating a made-up chalk winterbourne with a known answer, checking the dry spells and the losses by route, and fitting the well.
  • Reading the response gains comparisons over a year of rain: runoff ratio against soil wetness for every event; five soil stores scaled to the same quick flow, whose floods still differ; flow duration curves and the monthly baseflow index for each recharge rule; days to halve against flow; recessions from small and large floods overlaid; a fingerprint table of every option; and three mystery hydrographs as exercises.
  • The website has a light switch and opens in dark mode: navy for dark, warm cream for light. Figures adapt to the mode.

pdmS7 0.26.0

Fixes from a review of the compiled core, with the R reference changed to match. Results change only for models with the groundwater extension that use underflow, or that drain an adaptive cubic store by abstraction, and for lognormal soil stores whose inverse previously failed silently. Every other model gives the same results as 0.25.0.

  • The cubic store follows its solver with negative input. With the groundwater extension, an adaptive cubic store drained by abstraction switched to Smith’s method, whatever its solver. It now integrates the continuous equation through the moment flow ceases and on into deficit. From 1 mm with k = 1 and 1 mm/h net abstraction over an hour, it ends at -0.164 mm (flow ceasing after 0.836 h), where Smith’s step gives +0.367 mm. The Smith solver keeps Smith’s published steps.
  • Underflow is coupled with the main outlet. Underflow was held at its start-of-step rate, and its cap ignored the water leaving by the main outlet, so over a long step it could drain the store well below both outlets (from 10 mm with two equal linear outlets of 1 h over 2 h, to -4.5 mm). The store and both outlets are now integrated together, each outlet stopping at its own threshold within the step: the same case ends at 10 exp(-4) = 0.183 mm, each outlet releasing 4.908 mm.
  • The lognormal inverse proves convergence. It returned its last estimate after 200 iterations without checking it. It now returns only an estimate whose storage matches to 1e-12 (relative, at least 1 mm), and stops with an error otherwise.
  • Documented, not changed: the Smith solver’s accuracy limits (?cubic_routing), the meaning of a negative spring fraction (an import, counted as a gain in the water balance; ?groundwater_extension), the routing coefficient (q = S^m / kb, k = 1 / kb in the core), and four conventions of the implementation in the model equations article: evaporation before recharge, negative PET as condensation, discrete fractional delays, and interval-mean against endpoint flow.
  • New regression tests against closed forms and an independent fine-step integration, through the compiled core and the R loop.

pdmS7 0.25.0

  • One event per flood by default. find_events() now merges the events of one flood (independent = TRUE), as the calibration, the report, compare_calibrations(), the event workbench and batch_events() already did. Two peaks are separate floods only if they are at least separation (3) response times apart and the flow between them falls below trough (2/3) of the smaller. Code that called find_events() without independent now gets fewer, whole-flood events, and so do screen_events() lists, gauge_response() and the baseflow line behind water_balance()’s baseflow index. independent = FALSE gives the published method’s events, one per burst of rain, as before; the golden-file check against the reference code uses it.
  • The exponential store and PDM for PCs files: still to do. The structure recommendation keeps the exponential groundwater store among its options. write_pdm_inp() still refuses it, now with a message saying why: its layout in a PDM for PCs input file is yet to be confirmed. It will be added once an example file has been checked.

pdmS7 0.24.0

  • Which gauge the river answers to. gauge_response() takes each rain gauge on its own and correlates its rain with the rise in flow, lag by lag: the gauge with the strongest correlation drives the quick response. For the largest floods it names the gauge whose rain best matches each rise, checks whether each gauge sees the big storms as big, and counts the floods a gauge recorded almost nothing for. A negative best lag, rain after the rise it caused, flags a clock out. The slow response is not split this way: over days the gauges’ totals converge. Written up in Checking the data and the events.
  • Faster calibration. The compiled engine raises to the power 3 by multiplication, not by the general power function: a model run with the cubic groundwater store takes half the time (47 ms to 22 ms for eight hourly years), with the same results. Other structures are unchanged.
  • Starts side by side. calibrate_pdm() and calibrate_staged() take cores, and run the starts of a search in separate R processes, with exactly the results of running them one by one. calibrate_project() uses its cores for every search’s starts as well as for the structure comparisons, so two starts on two cores take about half the time. The default is the pdmS7.cores option, or 1.
  • The report shows how the structure was chosen. A new section draws the structure recommendation as a flow, one row per component: every option with its validation score, the choice, the equally good, the options set aside with a parameter at a bound and the option the step started from, with each step’s reason beneath. It is rebuilt from the log alone, so projects already calibrated get it on their next build_report().
  • Run totals in the report. Model runs and elapsed time for each structure step, each calibration stage and the project in all, with the seconds a run took.

pdmS7 0.23.0

  • The multi-zone PDM (PDM for PCs configuration guide, section 5): independent PDMs over parts of the catchment, driven by the same rain, their flows added at the outlet. A configuration with a zones list builds a FlodeMultiZoneModel; run_pdm(), calibration, projects, reports and compare_calibrations() take it like a single-zone model. Each zone runs on the compiled engine.
  • A fast zone for flashy catchments. two_zone_config() adds a small zone that makes quick runoff only (split recharge with alpha 1, one linear surface store, a groundwater store it never feeds). Every parameter is set; four are searched: its share of the area (0.01 to 0.3), soil capacity, surface time constant and delay. Bounds and exclusions without a zones. prefix apply to the main zone, so existing overrides carry over.
  • Zones in the structure recommendation. calibrate_project(recommend = TRUE, zones = c(1, 2)) and recommend_structure(components = c(..., "zones")) add a last step comparing one zone with two, by the usual rule: two zones only if better on validation by more than the tie tolerance and not pinned at a bound. zones = 2 adds the fast zone without a comparison. Forecast updating, hindcasts, the events workbench and PDM for PCs files stay single-zone.
  • The rain adds up across the zones. Each zone takes the catchment-average rain depth over its own area, and the zones’ areas sum to the catchment’s. The rainfall factor fc is one catchment-wide setting at the top of the configuration, locked at 1 by default and, if unlocked, searched as a single parameter for every zone. Giving it both at the top and in a zone is refused.
  • New article: the two-zone PDM. When one zone is not enough, how the fast zone is built and locked, a worked example on a made-up flashy catchment, and how to read the result.

pdmS7 0.22.1

  • A logo, in man/figures/logo.png, shown in the README and on the website.
  • Documentation reorganised. The calibration articles are fewer and say each thing once:
    • How automatic calibration works now holds multi-start, budgets and staged calibration (from the retired Calibration article), the objectives, including how the weighted stages differ from calibrate_pdm_multi()’s multi-objective trade-off, the locked rainfall factor and the split recharge bounds, and how the candidate is chosen.
    • How the model structure is chosen opens with how recommend_structure() chooses the recharge rule, soil store and groundwater store: the order, the rule and a worked example.
    • Getting the floods right explains how events are found (from the retired Events in large samples) and how to choose them by a flow, such as half QMED.
    • Many catchments: what automatic calibration recovers, and what limits it merges the large-sample article with the calibration study and the batch half of the events article.
    • Calibration records merges Logging a manual calibration and Inside the logs.
    • New: Comparing calibrations and PDM for PCs files.
    • Model options, model equations, scoring and the C core article cover the groundwater extension, thresholds from the record and interface version 3. The retired pages redirect to the articles that replaced them.

pdmS7 0.22.0

  • PDM for PCs input files. read_pdm_inp() reads the model of a PDM for PCs *.inp file into a configuration, and write_pdm_inp() writes one, following the manual’s conventions: the cubic store’s kb is the cube root of the time constant used, k2 = 0 means equal reservoirs, tdly may be given by its position, and the cubic store uses Smith’s method. The groundwater extension block and its well datum are read; the title, stations, events and optimised parameters are kept as attributes; error-prediction, rating and raingauge settings are noted, not used. The time step is not in the file, so it is an argument. Several hydrological zones, demand recharge, the power distribution and exponential stores are refused with a reason. The manual’s two example files ship in inst/examples.
  • compare_calibrations() runs two or more calibrated models, from configurations, YAML or *.inp files, or project folders, on the same forcing from the same start, and sets their parameters, scores by window, threshold scores against flow markers and errors on the largest floods side by side; plot() draws their hydrographs for a flood or a window.
  • calibrate_project() proposes the best fit in hand. It proposed the last stage whatever it scored, so a staged search that ended worse than the structure comparison’s own fit of the chosen structure threw the better fit away (seen on Beggearn Huish: calibration NSE 0.898 proposed over 0.936). The last stage is still proposed when it is within the tie tolerance of the best fit, so an events stage keeps its small trade; otherwise the best fit is, with the reason recorded in the candidate entry.
  • Split recharge is searched over 0.05 to 0.95 by default, not 0 to 1, so no search can switch a flow path off: at 0 every drop of direct runoff goes to groundwater and the surface stores carry nothing. overrides = list(recharge.alpha = c(0, 1)) restores the full range; the acceptance note on a path switched off now appears only at 0 or 1 exactly.
  • The groundwater extension runs in the compiled engine. Interface version 3 of the C core (src/pdm_core.h) adds an extension block to pdm_params and pdm_run_ext(), which takes an abstraction series and writes the extension’s five columns to their own table. pdm_run() and its 24 columns are unchanged. Simulation and calibration of extended models now use the core, which gives the R loop’s results exactly (checked for linear, quadratic, cubic and Smith stores through drawdown below zero, a dry spell and refill), at roughly 800 times the speed. The start from flow and state correction of extended models stay on the R loop.
  • Flow markers: thresholds from the record. flow_markers() works out QMED (the median of water-year maxima, as in the Flood Estimation Handbook), any multiple of it such as 0.5QMED, and flow duration exceedances such as Q1 and Q5. register_data() registers QMED, Q1 and Q5 when no thresholds are given (argument markers; NULL for none), so every catchment gets threshold scores; reports mark them as worked out from the record.
  • Events chosen by a flow. event_share in calibrate_pdm(), pdm_stages() and the project functions also takes a flow floor: a marker ("Q1", "0.5QMED"), a registered threshold’s name or a multiple of one, or c(peak = flow). Every event whose observed peak reaches it is then fitted, rather than the largest share.

pdmS7 0.21.0

  • Tier 1. The package is declared Tier 1 (experimental) under the Flode governance tiers: in CI and in every file header. Pull requests run only the test suite, on Ubuntu. The full Flode checks (R CMD check with the articles on four platforms, lint and coverage) run by hand from the Actions tab, until the package nears release.
  • The rainfall factor is locked during automatic calibration. calibration_bounds() leaves fc out, so calibrate_project(), compare_structures(), recommend_structure(), pdm_stages() and calibrate_batch() hold it at the configuration’s value, 1 in the presets. A calibrated factor absorbs the calibration period’s rainfall errors and carries them into operation, where the rain may come from other gauges or another product. Unlock it by giving it bounds, overrides = list(fc = c(0.8, 1.2)). Any other parameter is locked with exclude, as before. The bounds table gains a default column marking which parameters are locked by default. A run that searched fc before now gives different results unless that override is added.
  • The PDM groundwater extension, groundwater_extension(), as published in Moore and Bell
    1. and the PDM for PCs scientific guide (UKCEH, 2022, section 3 and Appendix B), for catchments with pumped abstractions, ephemeral streams and losses below or beyond the gauge. It wraps a linear, quadratic or cubic groundwater store and adds:
    • abstraction, A = cA + fA Ar, from a recorded series given as a forcing column abstraction (mm per step);
    • negative storage and flow cessation: the time to cessation within a step and the storage after it are the published Eqs. B.1 to B.6, checked against a fine-step solution (linear and quadratic exact; cubic by Smith’s method, as published, within 0.003 mm at 15 minutes); below zero the storage changes by continuity, and flow restarts once recharge refills it;
    • underflow, qu = (S + Dbu) / ku (Eq. 10), from the start-of-step storage like the model’s other losses, never below the underflow outlet;
    • external springs or inter-catchment exchange, a fraction alpha_b of the store’s outflow;
    • the storage deficit and well level, hw - Ys (Sbmax - S) in m (Eqs. 8 and 11). Set it in a configuration as groundwater: extension: {ku: ..., dbu: ...}. With nothing set it changes nothing: the flows equal the standard model’s. The water balance, losses included, closes to rounding. Its flow parameters are searched by calibration only when the configuration sets them, so a loss the record cannot inform stays off. The exponential store cannot be extended, since it cannot run dry, nor used with demand recharge.
  • Speed. A model with the extension runs in R, not the compiled engine: about 2.6 ms a step, so a 15-minute record of 17 years takes about 25 minutes a run. It suits checking and short records; the compiled version comes next, for calibration on long records.

pdmS7 0.20.0

Fixes from the Beggearn Huish calibration.

  • One event per flood. At 15-minute steps, with a response time under two hours, the event method cut a long flood fed by several bursts of rain into an event per burst. On Beggearn Huish seven of the ten “largest events” were slices of one flood, with event NSE down to -234, and the events stage of the calibration fitted that flood several times over: it lost 0.04 of NSE, 0.23 of log NSE and 16% of the water balance, and the peaks were no better. find_events(independent = TRUE) now merges events that belong to one flood: those whose flow windows overlap, and those whose peaks are not independent by the rule of UK peaks-over-threshold series (at least three response times apart, with the flow between them falling below two-thirds of the smaller peak; separation and trough set the rule). The events objective and the events stage, calibration_checks(), the largest events of the report, batch_events() and the Events tab of the app all use it. The default of find_events() is unchanged: the published method’s events, as checked against its reference code.
  • A flow path switched off is flagged. A lower bound of zero is usually a natural value, so calibration_checks() did not flag parameters there. A split recharge’s recharge.alpha at 0, though, sends every drop of direct runoff to groundwater and leaves the surface stores carrying nothing, as it did on Beggearn Huish, where it was reported as “No parameter at a bound”. alpha at 0 or 1 is now flagged, with a note saying what it switches off, and recommend_structure() sets aside a split recharge that ends there.

pdmS7 0.19.0

  • Progress during long calibrations. calibrate_project() said almost nothing between registering the data and the end, which on a long record is hours, so there was no telling whether it was running. It now reports its plan at the start; each structure step and each calibration stage as it begins; each structure’s calibration and validation scores and the time it took; and, after each structure step, the time left at the pace so far. During any search, calibrate_pdm() reports every minute or so how many model runs the current start has made (out of how many, for DDS) and how long each takes.
  • Comparisons on several cores cannot write to the console, so each structure’s progress goes to progress.log in the project folder, and the console says so.
  • options(pdmS7.progress_every = 0) turns the minute-by-minute lines off; any other number sets their interval in seconds.
  • Report fix. The candidate’s “Calibration window” hydrograph and flow-duration figures showed the validation window: the figures were drawn after the loop that made them, and every one saw its last window. Each window’s figures now show that window.
  • Report: the held-back wettest years each get a hydrograph of observed and simulated flow, once the test has scored them, beside the table of their peaks.
  • Report: the largest events. A table and a figure of the ten largest events of the record by observed peak, in whichever window they fall, with each one’s window, peak error, timing error and event NSE, and its rain.

pdmS7 0.18.1

Fixes from a review of 0.18.0.

  • calibrate_project() without a validation window now stops before the search when test years are registered, or the wettest years are held back (the default on a long record). The test scores a validated candidate, so before it failed only after the whole calibration had run. Give validation, or wettest_years = 0.
  • A rerun of calibrate_project() on a project that has a candidate now finishes whichever of the validation, the test and (with report = TRUE) the report are missing, instead of returning at once. A run interrupted after proposing its candidate can be finished, and a report added later.
  • recommend_structure() broke ties on the size of the median peak error, so errors of -50% and +50% cancelled to a perfect zero and beat a structure steadily within 10%. It now takes the median of the absolute errors. calibration_checks() reports it in its summary as median_abs_peak_error.
  • pdm_hindcast() spread its forecast origins from the first to the last row of the window, so a window with gaps, such as one leaving out held-back years, was forecast inside them too. Origins now fall only on rows of the window.

pdmS7 0.18.0

  • calibrate_project(recommend = TRUE) chooses the structure before calibrating. The structure given is the starting point; recommend_structure() then chooses the recharge rule, the soil store distribution and the groundwater store in turn, each by a structure comparison on the record, and the stages start from the calibration of the structure it recommends. Every comparison and every choice, with its reason, is in the project’s log. It needs a validation window and costs one calibration per option compared.
  • stages and bounds of calibrate_project() may be functions of a configuration, such as function(config) pdm_stages(config, events = TRUE), so that they suit whichever structure is chosen. New overrides and exclude arguments set the search ranges for the default stages and bounds and for every structure compared.
  • recommend_structure() gains overrides and exclude, passed to compare_structures().

pdmS7 0.17.1

  • New article, “Tailoring calibration to the largest events in the app”. It follows one project through the Events tab of calibration_app(), with screenshots: loading the largest events, reading their peak and timing errors, moving the surface stores and the time delay, saving the setting as a trial with a verdict and reasons, checking the recessions, refitting the other parameters from the trial on the Trial tab, and proposing and validating the result. The scripts that build the project and take the screenshots are in tools/app-screenshots.
  • Events tab fix. A slider rounds the run’s value to its step, so b = 0.439941 showed as 0.44. The tab took that rounding for a change: it reran the whole record, as for any change to b, and a saved trial recorded a change to b nobody made. A slider now counts as moved only when it is more than half a step from the run’s value. The event plots are also drawn at a higher resolution, so their labels can be read.

pdmS7 0.17.0

  • water_balance() checks the water balance before calibrating, for the whole record and for each water year (from October). Over a year a catchment stores little, so its loss, rain minus flow, is mostly evaporation, and two limits follow: flow cannot exceed rain, and the loss cannot much exceed the potential evaporation. Years beyond either limit are flagged, and so are years whose runoff ratio stands apart from the rest. A lasting change, such as a new rating from one year on, can leave no single year apart, so the years are also split at each boundary in turn and the largest change in the mean runoff ratio is flagged when it exceeds 25%; years already flagged on their own are left out of that test, so one bad year is not mistaken for a change. Steps with missing flow are left out of all three totals, and part years are reported but not judged. It also returns a double-mass curve and the baseflow index. plot() and autoplot() draw each year against the Budyko limits and Fu’s curve, the ratios year by year, and the double-mass curve.
  • The checks article has a new section, “Year by year: the water balance”, in which a new rating from one year on is found by the change test and seen in the double-mass curve. Its record now covers five whole water years, and its text on flagged parameters and peak errors is written from the results rather than fixed, so it stays true if the example changes.

pdmS7 0.16.0

Standard visuals, part 2 of 4: calibration and event plots.

  • Event plots. Event tables from find_events(), screen_events(), event_scores() and calibration_checks() now carry the class pdm_events, and plot() and autoplot() draw three standard plots:
    • balance: each event’s rain against its quick flow on log scales, with a dashed line at the runoff-ratio limit and grey lines at 0.5 and 0.1. An event above the limit shed more quick flow than the rain that fell, so the rain, the area or the flow is wrong for it.
    • peaks: simulated against observed peaks, with the 1:1 line and a 20% band.
    • timing: each peak’s timing error against its size. Screened events are drawn hollow; events from calibration_checks() are coloured by window.
  • Checks plots. plot() and autoplot() on calibration_checks() draw where each parameter sits within its search range, on the scale the search used, with any at a bound flagged; or the project’s events as above.
  • The calibration path. calibration_path() gathers a project’s automatic calibrations in order: each stage’s scores, every start’s result, and the candidate’s scores in each window. It prints a summary, and plot() and autoplot() draw the scores after each stage, each start’s objective, and the candidate in each window.
  • “Automatic calibration from start to finish” updated. Step 1 is now preparing and registering the data, with a flow diagram of the preparation functions; step 2 checks the data and the events; step 5 shows the check plots; a new section runs the same calibration in one call with calibrate_project() and plots its stages and parameters.
  • New article: “Checking the data and the events”. Every check in the order to run them: annual totals and the runoff ratio, each event’s rain against its quick flow, screening, parameters at a limit, peaks and timing, and the stages. A copy of the record with a mistyped area and an under-recording rain gauge shows each check firing.
  • Renderer. Hollow points, labelled axis positions, an x range, and score plots whose axis need not start at zero; the ggplot2 legends of mixed point and line plots merge.

pdmS7 0.15.0

The helper functions of the Beggearn Huish calibration script, tested and in the package.

  • Data preparation. read_hydro_series() reads hydrometric exports: split year, month and day columns in any of their spellings, one time column in the common formats, or a date and a time column, in any time zone; it refuses a file whose timestamps repeat. align_series() puts several series on one grid over the period they share. convert_units() converts mm per hour or day, metres, litres a second and megalitres a day, and with "auto" works the unit out from plausible annual totals. fill_gaps() fills by a named rule (stop, zero, interpolate up to a longest gap, none) and zero_negatives() sets negative values to zero. check_inputs() reports the period, gaps, negatives, annual totals and runoff ratio, and flags anything implausible.
  • Preparation in the log. Each of those functions notes what it did on the series it returns (preparation_notes()), and register_data() writes the notes into the registration entry; the report shows them in its Data section. Data registered without notes register exactly as before.
  • calibrate_project() runs a whole logged calibration in one call: project, registration, structure, staged calibration, candidate, validation when a window is registered and test when one is. A finished project is left as it is; an unfinished one is moved aside.
  • candidate_model() returns the model of a project’s candidate.
  • event_run() runs a project’s model over a separate event file: from the record’s own state when the event lies inside the registered record, otherwise from steady state at its first flow, with missing evaporation taken from the record. It prints the event’s scores and plot() draws its hydrograph.
  • calibration_checks() returns a pdm_calibration_checks list whose print method shows the parameters at a bound and the largest events in each window.
  • Article. The data preparation article has a new section running the same steps with these functions.

pdmS7 0.14.0

Standard visuals, part 1 of 4: the house style and the run diagnostics.

  • House style. Every standard plot uses the Okabe-Ito colours, which stay distinct with the common forms of colour blindness, and gives each colour one meaning: observed flow black, the model blue, rain sky blue, a second run or a change vermillion, the calibration and validation windows light grey and light orange, thresholds dashed reddish purple. pdm_colours() returns them by role for your own figures, and pdm_palette() gives a fixed order for series of equal standing. The previous palette’s green and red become almost identical to a reader with red-green colour blindness.
  • Base R and ggplot2. Each standard plot builds one description of what to draw, and two renderers draw it: plot() in base R and autoplot() in ggplot2, so the two always agree. ggplot2 is a suggested package: plot() always works, and the autoplot() methods register when ggplot2 is installed. theme_pdm() is the ggplot2 theme.
  • Figure sizes. pdm_save() writes PNG, PDF or SVG at standard sizes: screen, report and report_half (A4), slide (16:9) and journal_single and journal_double.
  • Run diagnostics. pdm_series() gathers a simulation with its observed flow, rain, windows, thresholds and an optional second run; project_series() builds it for any model entry of a calibration project. plot() and autoplot() draw a hydrograph with rain hanging from the top, flow duration curves, cumulative volume, or residuals with their 30-day running mean, over the whole record, a window or any period.
  • Restyled plots. plot_hindcast(), plot_recession() and plot_workbench() use the house style, and each gains plot() and autoplot() methods on its object. hindcast_scores() now returns a pdm_hindcast_scores data.table so that they dispatch. The workbench draws a trial in vermillion (it was orange) and observed flow in black; plot_hindcast()’s legend argument is kept but the legend now sits below the plot.

pdmS7 0.13.0

  • Events workbench. event_workbench() gathers a run’s n largest events (10 by default) in the calibration or validation window, screened with screen_events(). workbench_try() reruns them with parameters changed and scores each one; plot_workbench() draws them before and after. A change to the surface stores or the time delay reruns only the event windows, from saved states, exactly as a full run would; any other change reruns the whole record. The calibration app has a new Events tab: choose the number of events, move sliders for the surface stores, the time delay and b, and save the setting as a logged trial; a button draws the recession plot of the record and the model. The calibration log article has a new section on it.
  • Structure recommendation. recommend_structure() chooses the recharge rule, then the soil store distribution, then the groundwater store, each by a logged structure comparison on the validation window. Structures with a parameter at a bound are set aside; those within the tie tolerance of the best are equally good; the incumbent is kept when it is among them; otherwise the smallest median peak error on the largest validation events wins, then fewer parameters. Each step’s choice and reason is written to the log as a note. The choosing a structure article has a new section on it.
  • Catchment rainfall from gauges and radar. merge_rainfall() builds catchment-average rain by Thiessen polygons, multiquadric interpolation of the gauges (Hardy, 1971), or conditional merging of gauges and gridded radar (Sinclair and Pegram, 2005) with multiquadric surfaces: the gauges set the level, the radar the storm’s shape between them. rainfall_cross_validation() leaves out each gauge in turn and chooses the multiquadric shape parameter; catchment_mask() finds the grid cells inside a catchment boundary. Radar can be passed as a function returning one step’s grid, so a long record need not be held in memory. On a synthetic storm field, conditional merging matched the true catchment total within 1% with a correlation of 0.98, against 0.78 for Thiessen.
  • rainfall_field() gives one step’s rain field on the grid, for mapping a storm.
  • New article: “Catchment rainfall from gauges and radar”. Why rain is the main error, the three methods shown on a made-up storm (maps and cross-sections), checks at the gauges, over the catchment and through the river, and how to use H19 radar.
  • h19_radar() reads gridded H19 radar from the archive’s daily NetCDF files (either variable name, 2010 to 2019 or 2021 on), crops it to an extent and hands merge_rainfall() one 15-minute grid at a time, loading each day once. terra and ncdf4 are suggested packages.
  • New article: “Automatic calibration from start to finish”. The whole calibration in plain English, with flow diagrams: the record’s windows, the search loop, choosing the structure, the four stages, the checks and where each failure leads, the last steps and the log. A small calibration runs live through every step.
  • New article: “Getting the floods right”. A plain-English walk through why a good score can hide bad floods, and the tools against it: finding and screening events, the acceptance checks, the events stage, the workbench, recession analysis, what a record can tell apart about structure, and a suggested order of work. Its worked example runs live.
  • Can the record choose the recharge rule? inst/benchmarks/recharge_rules.R calibrates nine made-up catchments with standard, split and demand recharge. Validation scores found the true rule in all nine, by 0.08 to 0.25 in log NSE, against 0.003 for the groundwater store. Whether the baseflow line rises with each event’s quick flow separates split recharge from the other two without a model. The calibration study article has a new section on it.

pdmS7 0.12.0

  • Event screening. screen_events() flags events a hydrologist would not trust: a rise lost in the baseflow (small_rise: the peak rises less than min_rise times the baseflow beneath it), more quick flow than rain, gaps in the flow window, and peaks above the highest gauged flow. Every test works on flow above the baseflow line, so a high, steady baseflow is neither counted as event runoff nor mistaken for a rise. The events objective (event_screen) and calibration_checks() (screen) leave flagged events out by default, except peaks above the highest gauging, which are flagged but kept; in a project the registered highest gauged flow is used.
  • Events rerun on their own. event_states() runs the record once and saves the model’s state at the start of each event’s window; run_events() reruns only the windows, from those states. With the same model the result is exact. After changing the surface stores or the time delay, a lead-in five times the sum of the surface time constants brings event peaks within 0.1% of a full run; changing the soil or groundwater stores needs the states saved again, and run_events() refuses it. This is the groundwork for an events workbench and for tracing trade-offs between whole-record and event fit.
  • Recession analysis. recession_analysis() plots how fast flow falls against how high it is, from dry, falling steps long enough after rain, and fits the slope of that relation with a bootstrap interval over whole recessions. The slope identifies the groundwater store (1 linear, 1.5 quadratic, 1.67 cubic, 2 exponential) and the exponent of a power store. On made-up catchments it recovered every store where recharge stops between events (split recharge), but standard recharge, which keeps feeding groundwater through recessions, lowered the slopes by 0.1 to 0.9. So the slope is read straight only where recharge stops; otherwise compare the record’s slope with each fitted model’s, which plot_recession() draws together.
  • Can the record choose the groundwater store? inst/benchmarks/recession_stores.R calibrates sixteen made-up catchments with all four stores. The slope read from the record found the true store in 8, the closest simulated slope in 9, and the best validation score in all 16, but by a median margin of 0.003 in log NSE, below the 0.02 tie tolerance in 15. The calibration study article has a new section on it: compare stores, call those within the tolerance equally good, and keep the cubic store unless one is clearly better.

pdmS7 0.11.0

  • Calibrating for events. NSE over a long record counts time steps, not events, so a model can score well with its flood peaks late and low. Four additions guard against it:
    • calibrate_pdm(objective = "events") scores only the largest events, found with find_events(): 1 - pooled event NSE, plus the mean absolute peak error, plus the mean absolute timing error in response times, weighted by event_weights (nse = 1, peak = 0.5, timing = 0.5). event_share (0.5) sets the share of events, largest first, that count.
    • pdm_stages(events = TRUE) adds a fourth stage after the polish, which refits the surface stores, b and the time delay td (0 to td_max hours) on that objective with DDS (event_budget runs per start), leaving the water balance as stage 3 set it.
    • pdm_stages(thresholds = ...) puts a threshold term on the last stage, which then also searches with DDS. Stages may now carry their own method, control, threshold settings and extra_bounds (for parameters outside the bounds table, such as td).
    • calibration_checks() reports parameters that ended at a bound of their search range (a lower bound of zero excepted), and the median peak and timing errors and event NSE of the largest events in each window.
  • log_auto_calibration() accepts objective = "events" and records its weights and share.
  • The “Automatic calibration, explained” article has a new section, “Calibrating for events”.

pdmS7 0.10.0

  • Negative PE is allowed, as condensation. Potential evaporation products such as MOSES PE go slightly negative when condensation exceeds evaporation. Both engines, R and C, now accept negative pet (rain must still be nonnegative). A negative value is not scaled by soil wetness (Eq. 8): its whole depth joins the soil store, however dry the soil, since dew forms on surfaces whatever the soil moisture, and a full store passes it on as runoff, like rain. run_pdm(), register_data(), sim_pdm() and the calibration functions all accept it; missing PE is still refused. Results with nonnegative PE do not change.

pdmS7 0.9.1

  • find_events() has been checked against the authors’ reference code for DMCA-ESR, run in Octave, on three synthetic records (two hourly, one daily): identical response times and all 663 event windows identical. The help page and the events article record the check.
  • Fix: comparisons finishing within the same second no longer merge. compare_structures() named each comparison by its time to the second, so two on one project in the same second shared a name, and reading either back returned both. A suffix now keeps them apart.

pdmS7 0.9.0

  • Events from the records. find_events() finds rainfall-runoff events in continuous rain and flow records objectively, with the DMCA-based event separation routine of Giani et al. (2022): no baseflow separation, one setting (rain_min), any time step that resolves the delay between rain and flow. Each event has rain and flow windows, rain depth, peak, and with an area, quick flow and runoff ratio.
  • response_time_dmca() estimates a catchment’s response time from rain and flow alone (Giani et al., 2021). Ten years of 15-minute data take under a second, about twenty-five times faster than the R reference, which options(pdmS7.engine = "r") still selects.
  • The event method is in the C core, beside the model: pdm_dmca_rho(), pdm_find_events(), pdm_event_summary() and pdm_event_scores() in src/pdm_core.h, so Python, Scala and other languages find the same events as R. It matches the R reference exactly in event positions and within 1e-14 in every number. Golden files for three records (hourly, daily, and hourly with gaps) are in inst/golden/, checked from R, from plain C (tools/core/check_golden.c) and from Python (tools/core/events_example.py).
  • event_scores() scores a model event by event: peak error, peak timing, volume error and NSE over each flow window. batch_events() does it for every basin of a batch, labels each event with its window, and compares each basin’s observed and simulated response times.
  • New article: “Events in large samples: finding them and scoring models on them”.
  • synthetic_basins() at a sub-daily step no longer writes overlapping calibration and validation windows, which registration refused.
  • Fix: ar_from_response_time() refuses unstable AR sets. The default family’s first coefficient is set for 15-minute steps; at longer steps a decay of under about 4.9 steps gave a root of 1 or more, so the projected error grew without limit. At hourly steps that is any catchment with a time to peak under 4.9 hours. pdm_hindcast() used such sets by default without a word; it now leaves them out with a warning. Hindcasts of fast catchments at steps longer than 15 minutes change.
  • The AR article compares the model’s time to peak with the records’ response time (response_time_dmca()) as the family’s timescale. They forecast alike at 15 minutes; at hourly steps the records’ shorter timescale gives an unstable set more often and is no better where both work, so the time to peak stays the recommendation.

pdmS7 0.8.1

  • New article: “What limits automatic calibration: a study”. On 30 synthetic catchments, four searches are set against the score of the true parameters; the search reaches the best fit the record allows. Profiles show that kb cannot be recovered from flow records: across a hundredfold range it barely changes the flow, because the slow recharge hides it. It matters only in a drought long enough to stop recharge, where equally good calibrations can disagree by a factor of more than three in low flow.
  • The search results are stored as inst/extdata/search_study.csv; inst/benchmarks/search_methods.R regenerates them, including the staged search with the polish confined as before version 0.8.0.
  • With the free polish of version 0.8.0, staged DDS fits less well than staged L-BFGS-B in all 30 synthetic catchments (29 with the old confined polish); calibrate_pdm()’s help says so.

pdmS7 0.8.0

  • Staged calibration’s polish searches the full bounds. pdm_stages() used to confine stage 3 to a quarter of each range either side of stage 2’s values. Stage 1 fits with the surface stores at their starting values, and where the true stores are much slower it can settle on the wrong slow stores; the confined polish could not undo that. On 30 synthetic catchments it left two far short of their true parameters’ score (NSE 0.904 against 0.995 in one). With the full bounds, every catchment comes within 0.001 of the truth’s score. band still confines the polish when asked. Staged results change.
  • DDS. calibrate_pdm(method = "dds") adds dynamically dimensioned search (Tolson and Shoemaker, 2007), a derivative-free global search; control$maxit is its budget of model runs per start. It accepts threshold objectives, and calibrate_batch(), calibrate_staged(), compare_structures(), log_auto_calibration() and the app offer it. On the smooth NSE of the standard structure, L-BFGS-B remains the better choice: given the same number of model runs, DDS fitted less well in 29 of 30 synthetic catchments.
  • The large-sample article checks each calibration against the truth. Calibrations reach the true parameters’ score in almost every catchment, so a parameter that still comes back wrong (kb above all) cannot be recovered from the record, whatever the search. The article now calibrates all parameters at once.
  • inst/benchmarks/search_methods.R compares the searches on the large synthetic sample.

pdmS7 0.7.0

  • Large samples. synthetic_basins() writes a sample of synthetic catchments, each with its own climate and true parameters, as basin folders ready for calibrate_batch(), with each truth saved beside it. New article: “A large sample: what automatic calibration recovers”.
  • calibrate_batch()’s default structure takes each basin’s time step from its data, so daily and 15-minute basins need no structure of their own.
  • Parallel workers in calibrate_batch() and compare_structures() now use the main session’s library paths, so a package installed outside the default library (by R CMD build, renv or a user library) works with cores > 1; workers used to fail with “there is no package called ‘pdmS7’”.
  • read_projects() and batch_results() report wettest_score, the headline over the held-back wettest years.

pdmS7 0.6.0

  • The standard preset has a realistic water balance. It used to drain its soil to groundwater within a day (kg = 24 h), so the soil stayed nearly empty and evaporated about 2 per cent of potential. It now has a soil capacity up to 300 mm (cmax) and kg = 4000 h: evaporation about half of potential, baseflow index near 0.6. pdm_model()’s defaults and the parameter catalog match. Results from the preset or default models change; calibrations of real data, which set their own parameters, do not.
  • initial_state_from_flow() warns when a steady start would need more soil storage than the store holds; the soil is then capped and the run starts out of balance. This used to happen silently.
  • calibrate_staged() takes start and baseflow_fraction, like calibrate_pdm().

pdmS7 0.5.0

  • Extrapolation checks in calibration projects. Calibrations are fitted to the floods in the record and used for larger ones; this release makes that visible before sign-off.
    • register_data() holds back the two wettest water years (October to September) in the calibration and validation windows by default. No calibration, trial or validation scores them; test_candidate() reveals them once, with the test window, under the same rules. Set wettest_years to change the number, or 0 to hold none back. Holding years back needs a time column and enough record to leave three years, so short records now need wettest_years = 0.
    • Each automatic calibration keeps the parameter sets it tried that score within tie_tolerance (default 0.02) of its best headline, up to 50 spread-out sets. The test reports, for each held year, the observed peak, the candidate’s peak and the range across those sets.
    • register_data(highest_gauged_m3s =) records the highest check gauging. Flows above it, where the rating is extrapolated, are counted window by window at registration and flagged in the test. The fit is unchanged.
    • The report, the app and calibrate_batch() (through basin.yml) carry all three. Sign-off needs the test when years are held back, even without a test window.
    • Projects registered before 0.5.0 hold nothing back and reproduce as before.
  • Synthetic rivers. synthetic_catchment() builds a calibration problem with a known answer: stochastic rain drives a PDM with a lowland water balance, named storms can be added, and a simulated gauge records the flow with persistent (AR(1)) error and an optional rating bias above the highest gauged flow. synthetic_rain() generates rain and PET at any step by four methods: Neyman-Scott and Bartlett-Lewis rectangular pulses, a Markov chain with gamma amounts, and seasonal block resampling of a real record. fit_rain() fits the first three to a gauge record, including one read with reach.io; rain_statistics() gives the pulse models’ exact statistics; rain_parameters() the illustrative built-in values.
  • wettest_years() ranks the water years of any record by peak flow.
  • calibrate_pdm(archive =) keeps every trial’s parameters and a score of your choosing.
  • New articles: “Larger floods: extrapolation and the rating”, built on a synthetic river whose true peaks are known, and “Synthetic rivers: try everything on a known answer”.
  • The benchmark protocol is at version 0.3: a PDM-only extrapolation check on the wettest years, outside the head-to-head comparison, which holds no years back.

pdmS7 0.4.1

  • Calibration starts from the first observed flow. Every trial of calibrate_pdm(), and every run in a calibration project, starts in steady state at the first observed flow, so a slow groundwater store is full when scoring begins and cannot bias its own parameters. calibrate_pdm() gains start ("flow", the default, or "soil" for the earlier start), baseflow_fraction and start_flow. register_data() records the rule; projects registered earlier keep the soil start, so their recorded runs still reproduce. Calibrations will differ from those of 0.4.0 where the warm-up was short.

  • Locks on the calibration log and on shared CSV files recover from a dead session’s lock without the race that could delete a fresh one.

  • The run log and batch status refuse to append rows under a header with different columns.

  • validate_candidate() re-checks the candidate under the lock.

  • calibration_app() restores the identity options when it closes.

  • The C++ binding unpacks parameters in one place.

  • Six new pages on the website: “Where to start” (reading paths by role), “Preparing your data” (from EA sources through reach.io to model files, with a checklist), “Reviewing a calibration: a Steward’s guide”, a glossary, troubleshooting, and further reading. The home page states the package’s purpose, “Get started” opens the reading paths, and the roadmap is rewritten.

  • The benchmark protocol is at version 0.2, with its decisions closed.

  • Every source file is commented: the R package, the compiled core, the golden checker and the tests (each test states what it guards). A code review accompanies it, in code-review.md and under Guides on the website: no errors in the hydrology; two medium and seventeen low findings, ranked, with remedies for decision.

  • pdm_hindcast() reports “No forecast origins fit in the window” for a window too narrow for any origin, instead of an internal error.

pdmS7 0.4.0

  • New pdm_hindcast() reruns past forecasts from many origins, using the rain that fell, with no updating, persistence, AR post-processing as in IMFS (the Environment Agency 2024 default, a default-family set from the model’s response time, and optionally a set fitted to the calibration period) and state correction. hindcast_scores() scores each lead time: NSE, RMSE, bias, skill against persistence, threshold POD, FAR and CSI, and lead time over time to peak, so catchments and models line up on one axis. It also scores another model’s forecasts given as a table. plot_hindcast() plots any score against lead time.

  • New pdm_response_time() measures a model’s time to peak, recession and centroid lag from a pulse of rain, with an optional check against an FEH time to peak.

  • New ar_ea_default() and ar_from_response_time() give AR coefficients in the Deltares convention used by IMFS and reach.postproc; the second follows reach.postproc::default_family_ar_parameters() exactly.

  • New calibrate_staged() and pdm_stages() calibrate in stages: water balance and slow stores on log NSE with a volume penalty, then the fast stores on NSE, then a joint polish within narrowed bounds. log_staged_calibration() writes one auto_calibration entry per stage, each recording its stage; calibrate_batch(staged = TRUE) does the same per basin and resumes from the last finished stage.

  • calibrate_pdm() gains objective = "log_nse" and volume_weight, a penalty on the absolute volume error.

  • calibrate_batch() handles snow basins: with snow: true in basin.yml and a temperature column, PACK at fixed parameters turns precipitation into rain and melt, the PDM is calibrated on that, and a log note records the PACK settings and the raw forcing’s checksum.

  • New articles, “Testing forecasts with hindcasts” and “AR and ARMA error correction, explained”. “Automatic calibration” and “Calibrating many catchments” cover staged calibration and snow basins.

  • Internal: the calibration functions are split into smaller helpers; no results change.

  • The introductory articles are rewritten in plain English with figures of the model running: “How the PDM works” (buckets, dry and wet ground, the saturated area, the two paths to the river, the water balance, and what each setting does), “How the snow model works” (a winter, rain on snow, snow cover, settings, and snow with the PDM) and “Your first model run” (from data files to a calibrated, saved model). Each ends with a short equations appendix; the new “Model equations” page holds the full reference.

  • New write_pdm_config() writes a configuration that read_pdm_config() reads back exactly; general YAML writers round numbers to seven significant figures.

  • “Calibrating many catchments” is rewritten as a plain-English, step-by-step guide to calibrate_batch(), run live with an interruption and a failure. “Automatic calibration” is rewritten in plain English.

  • New calibrate_batch() runs one calibration protocol on every basin in a folder (each with forcing.csv, flow.csv and basin.yml), giving each basin its own calibration-log project, in parallel with cores. It can be stopped and restarted at any point: each basin carries on from its last completed step and finished steps are never repeated. Failures are recorded with their reason without stopping the batch. batch_status() shows progress from batch-status.csv; batch_results() collects the projects.

  • Three new articles: “Scoring a simulation” (every score, with the contingency table, event matching, events against steps and the performance diagram), “Automatic calibration” (bounds, log-scale search, the two optimisers and threshold objectives) and “Inside the logs” (project folders, entry files, the checksum chain, the run log and the register). The site’s articles are regrouped into Calibration, Records and review, and Forecasting.

  • New compare_structures() calibrates several model structures alike, in parallel with cores, logs each as a structure and an automatic calibration linked by a comparison id, and ranks them on the validation window, with optional two-way cross-validation. structure_comparison() rebuilds a ranking from the log. structure_set() gives the standard PDM and seven one-change variants; calibration_bounds() gives default bounds from inst/calibration-bounds.csv. The report and the app (a new Structures tab) show comparisons.

  • calibrate_pdm() and log_auto_calibration() gain log_scale, searching named parameters uniformly in log(value).

  • register_data() gains an optional test window, scored once by the new test_candidate() entry after every choice is made, and required before sign-off when registered.

  • New article, “Choosing a model structure”.

  • New article, “Calibrating many catchments”: one logged protocol applied to a batch of basins, budgeting, catching failures, judging scores as a distribution, checking whether multi-start runs agreed, and how well calibration recovers known parameters.

  • New read_entry() returns one calibration-log entry in full, and read_projects() gains validation_score, the candidate’s headline score on the validation window.

  • New threshold verification. pdm_threshold_scores() scores one or more thresholds at once: events (episodes above a threshold, merged across short gaps and matched within a timing tolerance) give probability of detection, false alarm ratio, critical success index and frequency bias, plus crossing time, peak timing, peak, duration and volume errors for each hit; a step-by-step count adds probability of false detection, equitable threat score and Peirce skill score.

  • register_data() gains thresholds (flows, or levels converted through a registered rating table and never extrapolated) and event settings. Every logged run is scored at every threshold, and a threshold score such as csi:Flood Warning may be the headline. The report adds a threshold table and a performance diagram.

  • calibrate_pdm() gains method = "nelder_mead", a derivative-free optimiser kept within the bounds, and an optional threshold term in the objective (thresholds, threshold_weight, threshold_score), or objective = "threshold" alone. log_auto_calibration() passes registered thresholds by name and records the method, objective and number of model runs. The default method and objective are unchanged.

  • New article, “Logging a manual calibration”: a complete project from start to sign-off, integrity checks and tampering, the report, and tracing operational runs with the run log.

  • New calibration_app(): a Shiny app over the calibration log for staff who prefer not to script. Setup (start, register data, select structure), Trial (adjust parameters, preview the hydrograph and scorecard against the parent, save with a verdict and reasoning; notes; automatic calibration), History (path, every run, compare two runs, propose and validate a candidate), Report (integrity, build and download) and Sign-off. Every button calls the exported function a script would, so the same rules apply. shiny is a suggested package, needed only for the app.

  • New opt-in run log. With options(pdmS7.run_log = "runs.csv") or PDMS7_RUN_LOG set, every run_pdm() call, and so sim_pdm() and sim_snow_pdm(), appends one row: who, when, an optional tag, the model’s pdm_fingerprint(), a checksum of the forcing, period, versions, run time, and success or the error message. Calibration evaluations, spin-up cycles and the calibration log’s own reruns are not logged. With a register of calibration projects set (pdmS7.register or PDMS7_REGISTER), each run is marked approved, superseded (its project was reopened) or unapproved; runs are never blocked. New read_run_log(), approved_configurations() and pdm_fingerprint(). Logging is off by default and a logging failure never stops a run.

  • New calibration log: an append-only, tamper-evident record of a calibration project. start_calibration_project(), register_data(), select_structure(), log_trial(), log_auto_calibration(), log_note(), propose_candidate(), validate_candidate(), sign_off_project() and reopen_project() each write one YAML entry recording who, when, which data and parameters, the scores and the reasoning. Entries are chained by MD5, data are copied and checksummed, and every run records a checksum of its output. verify_project() detects edits, gaps, changed data and runs that no longer reproduce. A Steward cannot sign off their own calibration. read_project(), project_trials() and read_projects() read the record. Design: calibration-log-design.md.

  • New build_report() writes a calibration report generated from the log: a self-contained HTML file with embedded figures, and a Markdown copy. It shows integrity status first, then data and scoring windows, model structure, the calibration path as a tree and a table, the candidate’s hydrographs, flow-duration curves and scorecard for both windows, parameter sensitivity on a shared scale, sign-off history, and the final configuration. It uses base graphics only.

  • New pdm_scorecard(): NSE, log NSE, KGE and its components, RMSE, signed and absolute volume error, peak error, and the Yilmaz et al. (2008) flow-duration-curve signatures.

  • Five new illustrated articles on the package website: choosing model components, starting states, calibration, forecast updating, and the C core. Articles, guides and the function reference are grouped by topic in the site navigation. DESCRIPTION gains URL and BugReports.

  • calibrate_pdm() gains opt-in multi-start calibration through starts and seed. Start 1 is the configured point; extra starts are drawn uniformly inside the bounds, all are optimised, and the best objective is returned. The result gains start_results, a table of per-start objective, convergence code, evaluation count and fitted parameters. The default starts = 1L runs the same single optimisation as earlier versions.

  • run_pdm(), and so sim_pdm() and calibrate_pdm(), now run a compiled time loop for every capacity distribution; standard, split and demand recharge; and cascade, power-law and exponential stores on either route. It is about 430 times faster. Output agrees with the R loop to rounding: bit-identical on R 4.3, with last-place differences on R 4.5 and later, where calibrated parameters can differ from earlier versions by about 1e-13 relative. options(pdmS7.engine = "r") forces the R loop, which remains the reference implementation. Building from source now needs a compiler (Rtools on Windows); cpp11 is a build-time dependency only.

  • Added inst/benchmarks/time_solvers.R and a report at docs/benchmarks/solver-timing.md timing both solvers and both engines on daily and 15-minute series.

  • pdm_model() (and so pdm_from_config() and sim_pdm()) warns, once per session, when the Smith cubic solver is used with a step above 1 hour. Its error grows with the square of the step and reaches 60 to 100 per cent of peak flow at a daily step. Results are unchanged; the default adaptive solver is unaffected. inst/benchmarks/smith_step_error.R reproduces the evidence.

  • The compiled time loop now sits behind a language-neutral C interface (src/pdm_core.h, interface version 2), so other languages can call the same model code. src/pdm_engine.cpp is a thin R wrapper over it, and results are unchanged. The core validates its own inputs and leaves the caller’s state untouched on error. tools/core/README.md covers building it without R.

  • Golden test files in inst/golden/ hold inputs and expected outputs from the R reference, for checking any binding of the core. tools/core/check_golden.c checks them from plain C.

  • The triangular capacity distribution is now inverted exactly (cube root or the trigonometric solution of a cubic) and the lognormal by safeguarded Newton iteration, in place of uniroot() with a 1e-10 tolerance. Storage round trips improve from about 2e-11 to 1e-14 mm; model outputs for these two distributions change by at most about 3e-11.

  • Fixed: the rectangular distribution’s capacity_mean() used (cmin + cmax) / 2 while its other methods used the Pareto b = 1 form, which can differ in the last place. A soil store filled exactly to capacity could then fail with “Soil storage exceeds capacity_mean”. Both now use the Pareto form, so capacity_mean() can change in the last place.

  • The PACK snowpack also runs in the compiled core, about 540 times faster than its R loop and bit-identical to it on R 4.3. sim_pack() and sim_snow_pdm() use it automatically. The core gains pdm_pack_run() for snow alone and pdm_snow_run() for snow feeding PDM.

  • New initial_state_from_flow(): a warm start in steady state with the flow observed at the start of a run. Routing stores deliver their share of the flow, the soil store is set so that recharge equals baseflow, and delay queues hold the water in transit. It replaces an arbitrary soil fraction for short test runs and forecasts. Also in the core as pdm_state_from_flow().

  • Forecast updating also runs in the compiled core: correct_state() (state correction, Moore 2007 Eq. 28-30) and update_forecast() (ARMA error prediction, Eq. 31-42), with pdm_correct_state() and pdm_update_forecast() for other languages. Results are bit-identical to the R code. Fitting the ARMA coefficients stays in R.

  • The compiled core is now plain C99 (src/pdm_core.c), so other languages need only a C compiler to build it. Results are bit-identical to the previous C++ version.

  • Fixed: the compiled engine rejected an initial state whose values were all stored as integers, for example one read with read.csv(). The R loop accepted it.

  • A peak timing objective is deferred.

pdmS7 0.3.1

  • Added three executable vignettes: PDM equations and functions, PACK snow accounting and defaults, and a synthetic calibration/validation/restart workflow.
  • Added reproducible process diagrams, soil/cover curves and workflow hydrographs.
  • No changes to the numerical model APIs or equations.

pdmS7 0.3.0

  • Added optional PACK S7 snow components, conservative substep accounting, areal depletion, fresh-snow memory and coupled PDM restart.
  • Added the image parameter preset (explicit hourly-unit assumption) and a distinct report-typical preset, with full parameter mapping and source notes.
  • Added multi-objective metrics, weighted multi-start calibration, evaluated Pareto trade-offs, configurable scales and joint snow/PDM parameter paths.
  • Documented river networks and additional state assimilation as future work.

pdmS7 0.2.0

Flode Tier 3 engineering target

  • Introduced Flode-prefixed S7 classes with existing class names retained as aliases.
  • Added sim_pdm() with explicit depth units, integer minute steps, data.table output, UTC timestamps, and warm-up flags.
  • Added safe YAML loading and an illustrative configuration file.
  • Replaced CSV input with fread() and tabular assembly with rbindlist().
  • Added state-object validation and structured debug logging.
  • Converted numerical regression checks to testthat and added interface tests.
  • Added roxygen source documentation, renv, lintr, and pinned shared Flode CI.
  • Retained the earlier simulation functions and output column names for compatibility.

This release targets the Tier 3 technical checks. It is not formally approved for operations: human maintainer attribution, independent review, and catchment validation remain required. Version 0.1.0 serialized S7 objects should be rebuilt from their saved configuration because the canonical class names have changed.
